row: CDP support posture **beyond** what S002 holds: the supported-products list, the `chrome.debugger` best-effort clause, API-stability conventions, and the trusted-client security assumption
Only listed official products are supported for direct CDP use, `chrome.debugger` is best-effort for developer-facing extensions, and protocol clients are assumed trusted
The normative semantics of robots.txt: what a robots rule does and does not authorize, 4xx/5xx handling, the 24-hour cache floor and the 500 KiB parsing floor
robots.txt is **not** access authorization: a 4xx robots response permits access, a 5xx means complete disallow

The agent-facing tool surface as shipped: the tool inventory per category, the per-category activation flags, and the journey-relevant semantics of `navigate_page`, `fill_form`, `wait_for`, `new_page` and `take_snapshot`
Every non-default category is flag-gated, and the shipped journey tools define their own semantics (e.g. `fill_form` is preferred over repeated `fill`)
The normative meaning of the rate-limit signal the lane records as a shape: status 429 and the `Retry-After` header
§4 "429 Too Many Requests" (and §7.2 security considerations); RFC 6585, April 2012
429 means "too many requests in a given amount of time"; `Retry-After` may state how long to wait, and a 429 response must not be cached

PDF §Abstract and §(2) 結果と考察; symposium 2025; opened and text-extracted 2026-10-23

on-change (the draft carries its own date)

The original paper's own findings on the Debugger API as an extension capability: the user-visible infobar raised on attach, the cancel button's effect, and the absence of rate-limit protection against immediate re-attach (arXiv preprint; no venue version opened)
§2.3 "User awareness" and §4 (attacks); arXiv:2305.11506, PDF v1 dated 2023-05-31; opened 2026-10-23
Chromium tells the user when a debugging extension attaches, but an extension can re-attach immediately, so the browser's notice is not a durable approval gate
The normative redirect semantics a journey driver observes (301/302/303/307/308, method rewriting) and the `Retry-After` header
301/302 MAY rewrite a POST to GET; 307/308 MUST NOT change the method; 303 redirects with GET or HEAD; `Retry-After` may accompany 3xx and 503
The normative cookie SameSite semantics that decide whether a cross-site submit carries the session cookie
§5.5.7 (The SameSite Attribute), §5.5.7.1 ("Strict" and "Lax" enforcement), §8.8 (SameSite Cookies); draft-13
Default enforcement is "Default"; Strict cookies are not sent on cross-site top-level navigations, and Lax is the CSRF-mitigating drop-in
